title: Diagnostic: Two-Phase Initialisation
hints: Phase 1 of class initialisation: a subclass sets its own properties **before** calling `super.init`.
Swap the two lines so `super.init` comes first.
jsBridge: **Two-phase initialisation**: a subclass must initialise its own stored properties *before* calling `super.init`. JS is the reverse: you can't touch `this` before `super()`. Swift's order guarantees no property is ever read uninitialised.

compass.q: JS requires `super()` before using `this`. Swift requires your properties *before* `super.init`. Why are they opposite?
Why can a superclass initialiser call an overridden method that reads a subclass property? What does phase 1 protect against?
Java lets the superclass constructor call an overridden method that sees uninitialised subclass fields. How does Swift prevent this bug?
Why do UIKit subclasses so often have `required init?(coder:)` with `fatalError`?
